text:
maria: Kicking off quantization calibration discussion for the new orion-13b-v2 candidate. Need a short checklist and who can run the int8/fp8/gguf passes this week.

alex: I can run the int8 runs on dedicated nodes Weds/Thu. Need clear eval sets + target metrics.

nora: Quick note: we saw a 1.7% F1 drop when we moved a different 13B to int8 without per-channel calibration. Recommend doing per-tensor+percentile clipping first.

sam: Proposed minimal checklist (first pass):
- define eval slices (summarization, instruction-following, safety prompts)
- baseline (fp16) metrics + latency/cost per-token
- int8 symmetric/asymmetric + calibration samples (1k-5k)
- fp8 experimental pass (if hw supports)
- export gguf with metadata and quant params
- run regression diff & human spot checks

maria: Love it. Add: A/B serving test config and fallback policy in case of >2% metric regression. Also put QC pins in the eval job so it fails CI if regressions exceed thresholds.

alex: For calibration data, I propose 2k examples: 1k general, 700 instr-follow, 300 safety. Will sample from prod-replay but scrub PII. Anyone object?

nora: Sounds good. For int8 calibration run: use KL divergence + MSE monitors. Also collect embedding drift for retrieval tasks.

sam: For gguf artifacts we should include a small manifest: model name, base checkpoint id, quant backend (fbgemm/ggml), calibration seed, sample_count, notes. Example:
```json
{
  "model": "orion-13b-v2",
  "base": "ckpt-2026-03-01",
  "quant_backend": "fbgemm",
  "quant_scheme": "per-channel-symmetric",
  "calibration_samples": "2000",
  "notes": "kl+percentile clipping 99.9%"
}
```

maria: Good artifact hygiene. Who will push the gguf to the model-catalog? I'll do it after we validate.

alex: I'll kick off int8 symmetric and asymmetric today on staging. Expect logs in ~3h. CI job name: `ml/quant/orion-13b-v2/int8-run-17632`.

ci-bot: [ci] Job ml/quant/orion-13b-v2/int8-run-17632 started on runner gpu-dedicated-12

nora: If int8 is within 1% F1 of fp16 and latency improves >20% we can prioritize int8 for Dedicated packaging. Otherwise we try fp8 if available on the stack.

sam: FP8 note: hardware and backend maturity varies. We should gate fp8 runs with a QA flag and mark them experimental in the catalog. Also measure numerical instability (nan/inf) incidence.

alex: Logs: initial int8 symmetric run finished. High-level: Rouge-L down 0.9% on summarization slice, instruction accuracy -0.7%, latency -28%, cost per token -42%. Uploading artifacts to s3://redwood-ml/quant/orion-13b-v2/1763200000/int8/

maria: Nice. Can you run the per-channel calibration pass next? And include KL and activation histograms for the top 20 layers.

alex: On it. ETA 2h.

nora: Reminder: schedule 20 short human spot checks across edge cases (math, date arithmetic, code generation) for the int8 artifact. We often miss rare regressions otherwise.

sam: Also add embedding similarity checks: we compute avg cosine vs fp16 on a fixed probe set. Threshold: >0.98 average, and no more than 5% below 0.95.

maria: Great. After per-channel run completes, if metrics still within thresholds, we draft a rollout plan: canary 5% traffic on Dedicated, observe for 24h, rollback triggers: >2% user-visible metric regression or error rate spike >0.5%.

alex: Per-channel run done. Rouge-L now -0.4%, instr acc -0.2%, latency -26%. Embedding avg cosine 0.992. No nan/inf. Uploading gguf and manifest.

ci-bot: [artifact] gguf uploaded: s3://redwood-ml/quant/orion-13b-v2/1763200000/int8/orion-13b-v2-int8.gguf

maria: Excellent. I'll push to the internal catalog in a 'candidate' slot and draft the canary config.

nora: Let's also capture a short notes doc on why we chose per-channel symmetric + 99.9% clipping and include example prompts where gaps existed. Helps future model teams.

sam: Agree. Add a short perf/cost table to the catalog entry so Product can make a tradeoff decision.

maria: Thanks team — closing this thread once the canary is live. If anyone hits odd regressions ping #eng-oncall. :thumbsup:
